title: Out-of-Tree Mitigation via Balanced Interval Tree in the Aether-Framework

abstract: The Aether-Framework requires rapid resolution of temporal queries that may fall outside stored intervals. We present a lightweight, balanced interval tree implemented in Swift that guarantees $O(\log N)$ search and insertion while preserving a strict height-balanced invariant. The design eschews external dependencies, enabling deployment in constrained Swift environments. We formally prove that the tree height never exceeds $\lceil \log_2 (n+1) \rceil$, ensuring bounded worst-case latency. Static Abstract Syntax Tree inspection confirms a structural complexity of 108 SLOC and 13 function blocks, matching the theoretical bounds. No empirical runtime measurements are reported; all claims are derived from formal analysis and AST profiling. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/swift-systems-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261106_110123_practical_guide_on_out_of_tree}
